title: Protocol 22 RestoreFootprint whose regenerated lake meta carries `restored` ledger-entry changes
why: LEDGER_ENTRY_RESTORED changes were added by CAP-66 in Protocol 23; a node at Protocol 22 reported a restore as created or updated entries. The lake's object for this Protocol 22 ledger was re-emitted by a Protocol 23 stellar-core, so the restore shows as two `restored` changes (the TTL and the contract data) in TransactionMeta v4, with backfilled fee events. Readers that branch on the ledger's protocol to decide which change types can occur, or that only know created/updated/removed/state, drop or mis-type the restored entries.

variants.notes: Real pubnet ledger at Protocol 22; the lake object is a regenerated re-emission.

values.note: LEDGER_ENTRY_RESTORED of the TTL, a Protocol 23 change type in a Protocol 22 ledger.
The backfilled refund event uses the per-transaction stage of pre-Protocol-23 refunds.

known_divergences.detail: txnbuild.TransactionFromXDR attaches the envelope's SorobanTransactionData only to InvokeHostFunction, so the parsed RestoreFootprint operation carries an empty Ext; the transaction rebuilt from the parsed object through txnbuild.NewTransaction (the rebuild fact) has no SorobanTransactionData and its own fee, and hashes to another transaction (ext differs).

notes: 300 transactions; the focus is the last one (apply index 299), the only RestoreFootprint and the only transaction of the Soroban phase. GCCNIZ6L… restores the persistent Balance entry of contract CBL3WJQR… keyed by its own address (value i128 0, last modified at 53378730) and its TTL (live until 57073653). It is charged 1620800: 1904256 in fee processing and 283456 refunded after apply; the backfilled refund event has stage after_tx (the pre-Protocol-23 refund point). The refund is in the bytes twice: the after_tx fee event of -283456 and the source account's balance in tx_changes_after (2076316967 → 2076600423). This regenerated Protocol 22 ledger carries TransactionMeta v4 inside a LedgerCloseMeta v1, which has no post-apply fee processing, so a reader must take the refund from tx_changes_after. The lake object was written by stellar-core 23.0.1 long after the ledger closed (source.regenerated true), so its TransactionMeta is v4 with backfilled classic and fee events, not what a node emitted at the time.
